question: Should OpenClaw add first-class per-agent backup/restore/clone in the core CLI now, and what security contract should govern copied credentials, session history, and clone identity rewrites?
rationale: The request crosses destructive state restore, credentials, transcripts, config mutation, and overlapping backup/migration work, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Design Core Per-Agent Restore
options.body: Keep this issue open as the narrow tracker and sponsor a core design for `--agent` and `--as` that reuses the current archive/snapshot model with explicit safety rules.

options.title: Fold Into Backup Umbrella
options.body: Treat this as a sub-scope of the broader native backup/restore issue and wait for that design to define the archive and restore contract first.

options.title: Defer Native Clone
options.body: Decline a core clone command for now and document manual or plugin-supported migration paths until a missing core API is identified.

recommendation.title: Design Core Per-Agent Restore
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the narrow tracker and sponsor a core design for `--agent` and `--as` that reuses the current archive/snapshot model with explicit safety rules.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent state/auth/docs work and the broader backup umbrella review make this the best available routing owner for the product/security boundary decision.
